title: DC-area forecast: Another stellar evening before warmth and humidity make a gradual comeback
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Mostly clear as late-evening 60s cool off to overnight lows in the mid-50s to low 60s.

What’s next? It turns warmer Wednesday and warmer still Thursday, while humidity slowly creeps back in. An approaching cold front brings the chance of an isolated shower Thursday and Friday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Mainly clear aside from periodic high clouds with slowly rising humidity. Lows range from the mid-50s in cooler spots north and west, to the upper 50s and low 60s downtown and south and east. A light breeze from the southeast calms during the evening. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Wednesday): Mostly sunny and warmer, with highs in the low to mid-80s. Dew points near 60 keep the slowly increasing humidity tolerable. A light breeze from the south may occasionally gust near 15 mph. Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Mostly clear and milder, with lows in the 60s for most of us. A light breeze from the south and southwest helps draw in warmer, more humid air overnight. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

We turn warmer still Thursday, with highs in the mid-80s to around 90 under partly sunny skies. Humidity edges up too, with dew points reaching the mid-60s. Maybe an isolated late-day shower or storm. Overnight lows settle mostly in the 60s, perhaps low 70s downtown. Confidence: Medium

A cold front approaches from the northwest and may stall nearby at times Friday into the weekend, bringing chances for isolated to scattered showers and maybe a thunderstorm, especially during the afternoon and evening. Otherwise, expect variably cloudy skies with warm, somewhat muggy highs mainly in the upper 70s to mid-80s. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for September 15

Intense late-summer heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 97 degrees, part of a prolonged hot and dry stretch during one of the region’s worst droughts on record.

Today's daily digit — 10/10: Wall-to-wall sunshine, refreshingly dry air, and highs from the mid-70s to around 80 — about as perfect as a September day gets. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
